question: What is used to remove permanent hardness of water?
solution:
The correct answer is __**Washing soda**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] __Key Points__

__
 
• Washing soda is chemically known as sodium carbonate (Na₂CO₃).
 
• It is used to remove permanent hardness of water, which is caused by the presence of dissolved calcium and magnesium salts.
 
• Washing soda works by reacting with calcium and magnesium ions to form insoluble carbonates, which can then be removed from the water.
 
• This process is known as water softening and helps in improving the effectiveness of soaps and detergents.
 
• Washing soda is also used in various household cleaning products and in the manufacturing of glass, paper, and textiles.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Baking Soda**

 
 
• Also known as sodium bicarbonate (NaHCO₃), it is commonly used in baking as a leavening agent.
 
• It is also used for cleaning, deodorizing, and in some fire extinguishers.
 
 
 
• **Bleaching Powder**
 
 
• Its chemical name is calcium hypochlorite (Ca(ClO)₂).
 
• It is used for disinfection, bleaching, and sanitizing purposes.
 
 
 
• **Sodium Hydroxide**
 
 
• Also known as caustic soda (NaOH), it is used in soap making, as a drain cleaner, and in the manufacture of various chemicals.
 
• It is highly corrosive and should be handled with care.
